fr: Je prends le bus pour aller au travail.
en: I take the bus to go to work.
ipa: /ʒə pʁɑ̃ lə bys puʁ ale o tʁavaj/
notes: The nasal an sound in prends is easy to mishear as a written d, but the final d is always silent.

fr: Le métro arrive dans deux minutes.
en: The subway arrives in two minutes.
ipa: /lə metʁo aʁiv dɑ̃ dø minyt/
notes: Deux ends in a silent x that is never pronounced, so do not add a sound you think you hear.

fr: Elle attend le tram à l'arrêt.
en: She is waiting for the tram at the stop.
ipa: /ɛl atɑ̃ lə tʁam a laʁɛ/
notes: Le elides to l' before the vowel of arrêt, so write l'arrêt as one joined word.

fr: Nous achetons nos billets au guichet.
en: We buy our tickets at the counter.
ipa: /nuz‿aʃtɔ̃ no bijɛ o giʃɛ/
notes: The nasal ending of achetons sounds like on, not ont, since this is a regular verb form, not avoir.

fr: Il y a beaucoup de voitures dans la rue.
en: There are a lot of cars in the street.
ipa: /il ja boku də vwatyʁ dɑ̃ la ʁy/
notes: The plural s on voitures is completely silent, so only the surrounding words show it is plural.

fr: Les enfants attendent le bus scolaire.
en: The children are waiting for the school bus.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ atɑ̃d lə bys skɔlɛʁ/
notes: Les enfants needs a liaison z sound linking the two words when spoken aloud.

fr: Tu descends à la prochaine station.
en: You get off at the next station.
ipa: /ty desɑ̃ a la pʁɔʃɛn stasjɔ̃/
notes: The final s of descends is silent, and the nasal en must not be written as an.

fr: Le train part à neuf heures.
en: The train leaves at nine o'clock.
ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ paʁ a nœv‿œʁ/
notes: Neuf heures liaises so the f of neuf is pronounced like a v before heures.

fr: Les passagers montent dans le wagon.
en: The passengers get into the train car.
ipa: /le pasaʒe mɔ̃t dɑ̃ lə vagɔ̃/
notes: The g in wagon is a hard g, unlike the soft g in voyage, so the spelling can mislead the ear.

fr: On prend le métro pour aller au travail.
en: We take the subway to go to work.
ipa: /ɔ̃ pʁɑ̃ lə metʁo puʁ ale o tʁavaj/
notes: On here is the pronoun spelled o-n, easily confused by sound with ont from the verb avoir.

fr: Le bus est en retard ce matin.
en: The bus is late this morning.
ipa: /lə bys ɛt‿ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ sə matɛ̃/
notes: Est en carries a hidden liaison t sound linking the two words, easy to miss when writing.

fr: Nous marchons jusqu'à la gare.
en: We walk to the station.
ipa: /nu maʁʃɔ̃ ʒyska la gaʁ/
notes: Jusqu'à is one elided word combining jusque and à, never written as two separate words.

fr: Les rues sont pleines de monde à cette heure.
en: The streets are full of people at this hour.
ipa: /le ʁy sɔ̃ plɛn də mɔ̃d a sɛt œʁ/
notes: Cette drops its final mute e sound before the vowel of heure, so the two words run together.

fr: Le conducteur ferme les portes du bus.
en: The driver closes the bus doors.
ipa: /lə kɔ̃dyktœʁ fɛʁm le pɔʁt dy bys/
notes: The plural portes adds a silent s that changes nothing in pronunciation, so rely on les for the plural clue.

fr: J'attends le prochain train sur le quai.
en: I am waiting for the next train on the platform.
ipa: /ʒatɑ̃ lə pʁɔʃɛ̃ tʁɛ̃ syʁ lə kɛ/
notes: J'attends elides je before the vowel-starting verb, written as one word with an apostrophe.

fr: Il fait beau, alors je prends mon vélo.
en: It's nice out, so I'm taking my bike.
ipa: /il fɛ bo alɔʁ ʒə pʁɑ̃ mɔ̃ velo/
notes: Mon keeps a nasal on sound that must stay nasal and never be written as mont.

fr: La station de métro est fermée aujourd'hui.
en: The subway station is closed today.
ipa: /la stasjɔ̃ də metʁo ɛ fɛʁme oʒuʁdɥi/
notes: Aujourd'hui hides a silent d and an elided article, so its short spoken form does not match its long spelling.

fr: Elle traverse la rue au feu rouge.
en: She crosses the street at the red light.
ipa: /ɛl tʁavɛʁs la ʁy o fø ʁuʒ/
notes: The final e of rouge is silent, so the word ends on the soft j sound, not a vowel.

fr: Nous attendons le bus sous la pluie.
en: We are waiting for the bus in the rain.
ipa: /nuz‿atɑ̃dɔ̃ lə bys su la plɥi/
notes: Nous attendons liaises the final s of nous into a z sound before the vowel of attendons.

fr: Le vélo est garé devant l'école.
en: The bike is parked in front of the school.
ipa: /lə velo ɛ gaʁe dəvɑ̃ lekɔl/
notes: L'école elides le before the vowel, so never write le école as two separate words.

fr: Les enfants montent dans le bus jaune.
en: The children get on the yellow bus.
ipa: /lez‿ɑ̃fɑ̃ mɔ̃t dɑ̃ lə bys ʒon/
notes: Les enfants needs the liaison z, blending les and enfants into one sound group.

fr: Le chauffeur conduit lentement dans le brouillard.
en: The driver drives slowly in the fog.
ipa: /lə ʃofœʁ kɔ̃dɥi lɑ̃tmɑ̃ dɑ̃ lə bʁujaʁ/
notes: The double f in chauffeur is pronounced as a single f sound, so do not stretch the sound when writing.

fr: Tu attends tes amis à l'arrêt de bus.
en: You are waiting for your friends at the bus stop.
ipa: /ty atɑ̃ tez‿ami a laʁɛ də bys/
notes: Tes amis liaises so the final s of tes sounds like z before the vowel of amis.

fr: Le train arrive dans dix minutes.
en: The train arrives in ten minutes.
ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ aʁiv dɑ̃ di minyt/
notes: Dix drops its final consonant sound before minutes, so it is pronounced like di, not dix as spelled.

fr: Elle prend toujours le même chemin.
en: She always takes the same path.
ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ tuʒuʁ lə mɛm ʃəmɛ̃/
notes: Chemin ends in a nasal in sound that must be written in, not the ain ending that sounds the same.

fr: Nous montons dans le tramway numéro trois.
en: We get on tram number three.
ipa: /nu mɔ̃tɔ̃ dɑ̃ lə tʁamwɛ nymeʁo tʁwa/
notes: Tramway keeps a French nasal am sound, so it is not pronounced the English way despite its spelling.

fr: Le taxi attend devant l'hôtel.
en: The taxi is waiting in front of the hotel.
ipa: /lə taksi atɑ̃ dəvɑ̃ lotɛl/
notes: L'hôtel elides le before the silent h, since h is never pronounced in French.

fr: Les feux sont rouges au carrefour.
en: The lights are red at the intersection.
ipa: /le fø sɔ̃ ʁuʒ o kaʁfuʁ/
notes: Feux ends in a silent x, so the plural sounds identical to the singular feu.

fr: Je marche vite pour ne pas rater le bus.
en: I walk fast so I don't miss the bus.
ipa: /ʒə maʁʃ vit puʁ nə pa ʁate lə bys/
notes: Rater ends in the er sound shared by many infinitives, easy to confuse with a past participle when writing.

fr: Le vélo roule vite dans la piste cyclable.
en: The bike rides fast on the bike path.
ipa: /lə velo ʁul vit dɑ̃ la pist siklabl/
notes: The c in cyclable is pronounced like an s before y, not like the k sound in vélo.

fr: Ils attendent le métro sur le quai.
en: They are waiting for the subway on the platform.
ipa: /ilz‿atɑ̃d lə metʁo syʁ lə kɛ/
notes: Ils attendent liaises the final s of ils into a z sound before the vowel of attendent.

fr: Le prix du billet est affiché au guichet.
en: The price of the ticket is displayed at the counter.
ipa: /lə pʁi dy bijɛ ɛt‿afiʃe o giʃɛ/
notes: Est affiché liaises the t of est into the following vowel, so the two words blend together.

fr: Nous descendons à la station suivante.
en: We get off at the next stop.
ipa: /nu desɑ̃dɔ̃ a la stasjɔ̃ sɥivɑ̃t/
notes: Suivante keeps a silent final e after the pronounced t, marking the feminine form without changing the sound.

fr: Le bus numéro sept passe toutes les dix minutes.
en: Bus number seven comes every ten minutes.
ipa: /lə bys nymeʁo sɛt pas tut le di minyt/
notes: Sept pronounces its final t here, unlike dix later in the sentence which loses its final consonant.

fr: Elle achète un ticket de métro.
en: She buys a subway ticket.
ipa: /ɛl aʃɛt œ̃ tikɛ də metʁo/
notes: Un is a nasal vowel sound, never pronounced like une, so keep the two forms distinct when writing.

fr: Les touristes cherchent la bonne sortie.
en: The tourists are looking for the right exit.
ipa: /le tuʁist ʃɛʁʃ la bɔn sɔʁti/
notes: Bonne doubles its n and keeps a sounded final e, unlike the masculine bon which sounds nasal.

fr: Le bus s'arrête devant la boulangerie.
en: The bus stops in front of the bakery.
ipa: /lə bys saʁɛt dəvɑ̃ la bulɑ̃ʒʁi/
notes: S'arrête elides se before the vowel-starting verb, forming one written word with an apostrophe.

fr: Les gens courent pour attraper le train.
en: People run to catch the train.
ipa: /le ʒɑ̃ kuʁ puʁ atʁape lə tʁɛ̃/
notes: Gens ends in a nasal sound spelled ens, easy to confuse with the ans ending that sounds identical.

fr: Le parking est complet ce soir.
en: The parking lot is full tonight.
ipa: /lə paʁkiŋ ɛ kɔ̃plɛ sə swaʁ/
notes: Parking is a borrowed word whose final g is pronounced as a nasal ng sound, not a hard g.

fr: Nous prenons le premier train du matin.
en: We take the first train of the morning.
ipa: /nu pʁənɔ̃ lə pʁəmje tʁɛ̃ dy matɛ̃/
notes: Premier ends in a nasal sound spelled ier, not to be confused with a plain e sound.

fr: Le conducteur klaxonne à cause des embouteillages.
en: The driver honks because of the traffic jams.
ipa: /lə kɔ̃dyktœʁ klaksɔn a koz dez‿ɑ̃butɛjaʒ/
notes: Des embouteillages liaises the s of des into a z sound before the vowel of embouteillages.

fr: Elle roule à vélo même quand il pleut.
en: She rides her bike even when it rains.
ipa: /ɛl ʁul a velo mɛm kɑ̃t‿il plø/
notes: Quand il liaises the silent d of quand into a t sound before the vowel of il.

fr: Le quai est plein de voyageurs.
en: The platform is full of travelers.
ipa: /lə kɛ ɛ plɛ̃ də vwajaʒœʁ/
notes: Plein is a nasal vowel spelled ein, distinct in spelling from the ain that sounds the same.

fr: Les portes du métro se ferment vite.
en: The subway doors close quickly.
ipa: /le pɔʁt dy metʁo sə fɛʁm vit/
notes: The verb ending ent in ferment is completely silent, so the plural agreement with les portes is invisible in speech.

fr: Le chemin le plus court passe par le parc.
en: The shortest path goes through the park.
ipa: /lə ʃəmɛ̃ lə ply kuʁ pas paʁ lə paʁk/
notes: Plus drops its final s sound here before a consonant, unlike when it means more and the s can be heard.

fr: Nous cherchons la station de métro la plus proche.
en: We are looking for the nearest subway station.
ipa: /nu ʃɛʁʃɔ̃ la stasjɔ̃ də metʁo la ply pʁɔʃ/
notes: Cherchons ends in the silent nasal ons sound, not to be confused with the word son.

fr: Le vélo est moins cher que la voiture.
en: The bike is cheaper than the car.
ipa: /lə velo ɛ mwɛ̃ ʃɛʁ kə la vwatyʁ/
notes: Moins is a nasal vowel ending in a silent s that is never pronounced in this fixed expression.

fr: Les vélos en libre-service sont pratiques en ville.
en: Bike-share bikes are practical in the city.
ipa: /le veloz‿ɑ̃ libʁəsɛʁvis sɔ̃ pʁatik ɑ̃ vil/
notes: Vélos en liaises the s of vélos into a z sound before the vowel of en.

fr: Le tramway s'arrête à chaque coin de rue.
en: The tram stops at every street corner.
ipa: /lə tʁamwɛ saʁɛt a ʃak kwɛ̃ də ʁy/
notes: S'arrête is one elided word joining se and arrête, never written as two separate words.

fr: Elle marche jusqu'au bureau chaque jour.
en: She walks to the office every day.
ipa: /ɛl maʁʃ ʒysko byʁo ʃak ʒuʁ/
notes: Jusqu'au contracts jusque, à, and le into one written word before a masculine noun.

fr: Le bus est bondé aux heures de pointe.
en: The bus is crowded during rush hour.
ipa: /lə bys ɛ bɔ̃de oz‿œʁ də pwɛ̃t/
notes: Aux heures liaises the x of aux into a z sound before the vowel of heures.

fr: Les voyageurs attendent patiemment sur le quai.
en: The travelers wait patiently on the platform.
ipa: /le vwajaʒœʁ atɑ̃d pasjamɑ̃ syʁ lə kɛ/
notes: Patiemment hides a t pronounced as s and a nasal ending that does not match its emment spelling.

fr: Hier, j'ai pris le bus pour aller au travail.
en: Yesterday, I took the bus to go to work.
ipa: /jɛʁ ʒe pʁi lə bys puʁ ale o tʁavaj/
notes: J'ai pris is passé composé with avoir, and pris never agrees since there is no preceding direct object.

fr: Elle est montée dans le train à huit heures.
en: She got on the train at eight o'clock.
ipa: /ɛl ɛ mɔ̃te dɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃ a ɥit œʁ/
notes: Montée agrees with the feminine subject elle and adds a silent e, since monter takes être.

fr: Nous avons manqué notre correspondance à la gare.
en: We missed our connection at the station.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ mɑ̃ke nɔtʁ kɔʁɛspɔ̃dɑ̃s a la gaʁ/
notes: Manqué ends like the infinitive manquer but is a past participle here, since both sound identical as é.

fr: Il va prendre le métro demain matin.
en: He is going to take the subway tomorrow morning.
ipa: /il va pʁɑ̃dʁ lə metʁo dəmɛ̃ matɛ̃/
notes: Va prendre is futur proche, so prendre stays in the infinitive and is never conjugated after aller.

fr: Les passagers sont arrivés en retard à cause des travaux.
en: The passengers arrived late because of the roadwork.
ipa: /le pasaʒe sɔ̃t‿aʁive ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ a koz de tʁavo/
notes: Sont arrivés agrees in the plural with an added silent s, since arriver takes être and passagers is plural.

fr: J'ai acheté un abonnement mensuel pour le tram.
en: I bought a monthly pass for the tram.
ipa: /ʒe aʃte œ̃n‿abɔnmɑ̃ mɑ̃sɥɛl puʁ lə tʁam/
notes: Acheté and acheter sound identical when spoken, so only j'ai before it signals the past participle.

fr: On a attendu le bus pendant vingt minutes.
en: We waited for the bus for twenty minutes.
ipa: /ɔ̃n‿a atɑ̃dy lə bys pɑ̃dɑ̃ vɛ̃ minyt/
notes: On a sounds exactly like on n'a or like ont, so only the sentence meaning tells them apart.

fr: Elle a pris son vélo parce qu'il faisait beau.
en: She took her bike because it was nice out.
ipa: /ɛl a pʁi sɔ̃ velo paʁskil fəzɛ bo/
notes: A pris can be confused by ear with appris, so listen carefully to the vowel sound after the a.

fr: Nous sommes allés à la gare en taxi.
en: We went to the station by taxi.
ipa: /nu sɔmz‿ale a la gaʁ ɑ̃ taksi/
notes: Allés agrees with the plural subject nous, adding a silent s that changes nothing in pronunciation.

fr: Le train va partir dans cinq minutes.
en: The train is going to leave in five minutes.
ipa: /lə tʁɛ̃ va paʁtiʁ dɑ̃ sɛ̃k minyt/
notes: Va partir uses the futur proche, so partir keeps its infinitive ending and is not conjugated.

fr: Ils ont raté le dernier métro hier soir.
en: They missed the last subway last night.
ipa: /ilz‿ɔ̃ ʁate lə dɛʁnje metʁo jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: Ont here is the verb avoir, easily confused by ear with the pronoun on, so context decides the spelling.

fr: Elle a validé son ticket avant de monter.
en: She validated her ticket before getting on.
ipa: /ɛl a valide sɔ̃ tikɛ avɑ̃ də mɔ̃te/
notes: Validé ends in a silent e after the past participle sound, since there is no preceding direct object to agree with.

fr: Nous avons pris un taxi parce qu'il pleuvait.
en: We took a taxi because it was raining.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ pʁiz‿œ̃ taksi paʁskil pløvɛ/
notes: Pris un carries a liaison z sound linking the past participle to un, so the two words blend when spoken.

fr: Vous avez acheté vos billets en ligne, n'est-ce pas ?
en: You bought your tickets online, didn't you?
ipa: /vuz‿ave aʃte vo bijɛ ɑ̃ liɲ nɛskə pa/
notes: Billets keeps a silent final s for the plural that is never heard in speech.

fr: Le bus a klaxonné avant de partir.
en: The bus honked before leaving.
ipa: /lə bys a klaksɔne avɑ̃ də paʁtiʁ/
notes: Klaxonné is a past participle sounding just like the infinitive klaxonner, so grammar alone tells them apart.

fr: Nous avons couru pour attraper la correspondance.
en: We ran to catch the connection.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ kuʁy puʁ atʁape la kɔʁɛspɔ̃dɑ̃s/
notes: Couru is an irregular past participle that does not end in the usual é sound, so it must be memorized.

fr: Elle va acheter un ticket au distributeur.
en: She is going to buy a ticket at the machine.
ipa: /ɛl va aʃte œ̃ tikɛ o distʁibytœʁ/
notes: Va acheter is futur proche, keeping acheter as an infinitive rather than adding a personal ending.

fr: Ils sont partis tôt pour éviter les embouteillages.
en: They left early to avoid the traffic jams.
ipa: /il sɔ̃ paʁti to puʁ evite lez‿ɑ̃butɛjaʒ/
notes: Partis agrees with the masculine plural subject ils, adding a silent s since partir takes être.

fr: On a vu le bus partir sans nous.
en: We saw the bus leave without us.
ipa: /ɔ̃n‿a vy lə bys paʁtiʁ sɑ̃ nu/
notes: On a and on n'a pas sound very close, so a missing negation changes the whole meaning.

fr: J'ai marché jusqu'à la gare parce que le bus était en panne.
en: I walked to the station because the bus had broken down.
ipa: /ʒe maʁʃe ʒyska la gaʁ paʁskə lə bys etɛt‿ɑ̃ pan/
notes: Marché as a past participle sounds identical to the noun marché meaning market, so context decides the meaning.

fr: Nous avons pris le train plutôt que la voiture.
en: We took the train rather than the car.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ pʁi lə tʁɛ̃ plyto kə la vwatyʁ/
notes: Plutôt is one word meaning rather, easily confused in writing with plus tôt meaning earlier.

fr: Elle est descendue à la mauvaise station.
en: She got off at the wrong station.
ipa: /ɛl ɛ desɑ̃dy a la movɛz stasjɔ̃/
notes: Descendue agrees with the feminine elle, adding a silent e since descendre takes être.

fr: Vous avez réservé vos places dans le train ?
en: Did you reserve your seats on the train?
ipa: /vuz‿ave ʁezɛʁve vo plas dɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃/
notes: Réservé sounds exactly like the infinitive réserver, so only avez before it signals the past participle.

fr: Nous allons prendre le premier métro du matin.
en: We are going to take the first subway of the morning.
ipa: /nuz‿alɔ̃ pʁɑ̃dʁ lə pʁəmje metʁo dy matɛ̃/
notes: Allons prendre is futur proche, so prendre remains an infinitive and never takes a conjugated ending.

fr: Le tram est passé sans s'arrêter à cet arrêt.
en: The tram went by without stopping at this stop.
ipa: /lə tʁam ɛ pase sɑ̃ saʁete a sɛt aʁɛ/
notes: Est passé agrees with the masculine singular subject tram, taking a simple é with no extra letter.

fr: Ils ont oublié leurs billets à la maison.
en: They forgot their tickets at home.
ipa: /ilz‿ɔ̃t‿ublije lœʁ bijɛ a la mɛzɔ̃/
notes: Ont oublié liaises the t of ont into the vowel of oublié, so the two words blend into one sound group.

fr: Nous avons attendu longtemps sur le quai.
en: We waited a long time on the platform.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ atɑ̃dy lɔ̃tɑ̃ syʁ lə kɛ/
notes: Longtemps ends in a silent p and s together, so its spoken form is much shorter than its spelling suggests.

fr: Elle a pris un aller-retour pour le week-end.
en: She bought a round-trip ticket for the weekend.
ipa: /ɛl a pʁiz‿œ̃n‿ale ʁətuʁ puʁ lə wikɛnd/
notes: Aller-retour hides two liaisons, and the compound noun stays invariable in most everyday uses.

fr: Le chauffeur a freiné brusquement au feu rouge.
en: The driver braked suddenly at the red light.
ipa: /lə ʃofœʁ a fʁene bʁyskəmɑ̃ o fø ʁuʒ/
notes: Freiné is a past participle that sounds just like the infinitive freiner, distinguished only by the helping verb a.

fr: Nous sommes arrivés à l'heure malgré la grève.
en: We arrived on time despite the strike.
ipa: /nu sɔmz‿aʁivez‿a lœʁ malgʁe la gʁɛv/
notes: Arrivés agrees with the plural nous, and the following liaison links arrivés to à l'heure smoothly.

fr: Elle va prendre un taxi si elle rate le bus.
en: She is going to take a taxi if she misses the bus.
ipa: /ɛl va pʁɑ̃dʁ œ̃ taksi si ɛl ʁat lə bys/
notes: Va prendre keeps prendre in its infinitive form, since futur proche never adds a personal verb ending.

fr: Ont-ils composté leurs billets avant de monter ?
en: Did they validate their tickets before boarding?
ipa: /ɔ̃til kɔ̃pɔste lœʁ bijɛ avɑ̃ də mɔ̃te/
notes: Ont-ils is the verb avoir inverted with ils, and its spelling depends on grammar, not on how it sounds.

fr: Nous avons roulé à vélo malgré la pluie.
en: We rode our bikes despite the rain.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ ʁule a velo malgʁe la plɥi/
notes: Roulé is invariable here since rouler takes avoir and there is no preceding direct object to agree with.

fr: Le métro va s'arrêter à la station suivante.
en: The subway is going to stop at the next station.
ipa: /lə metʁo va saʁete a la stasjɔ̃ sɥivɑ̃t/
notes: Va s'arrêter keeps the reflexive infinitive intact after aller, never conjugating arrêter itself.

fr: Elles sont montées à l'avant du bus.
en: They got on at the front of the bus.
ipa: /ɛl sɔ̃ mɔ̃tez‿a lavɑ̃ dy bys/
notes: Montées agrees with the feminine plural elles, adding a silent es that liaises before the following vowel.

fr: J'ai loué un vélo pour la journée.
en: I rented a bike for the day.
ipa: /ʒe lwe œ̃ velo puʁ la ʒuʁne/
notes: Loué sounds identical to louer, the infinitive, so only j'ai signals a completed action.

fr: Nous avons dû changer de quai à la dernière minute.
en: We had to change platforms at the last minute.
ipa: /nuz‿avɔ̃ dy ʃɑ̃ʒe də kɛ a la dɛʁnjɛʁ minyt/
notes: Dû keeps its circumflex accent to distinguish it in writing from du, the contracted article, though both sound similar.

fr: Ils vont prendre le bus ou le tram, ils ne savent pas encore.
en: They are going to take the bus or the tram, they don't know yet.
ipa: /il vɔ̃ pʁɑ̃dʁ lə bys u lə tʁam il nə sav pa ɑ̃kɔʁ/
notes: Ou meaning or has no accent, unlike où meaning where, though the two words sound exactly the same.

fr: Où est la station de métro la plus proche d'ici ?
en: Where is the nearest subway station from here?
ipa: /u ɛ la stasjɔ̃ də metʁo la ply pʁɔʃ disi/
notes: Où meaning where carries an accent grave to distinguish it from ou meaning or, even though both sound identical.

fr: Ce chauffeur se plaint souvent des embouteillages.
en: This driver often complains about the traffic jams.
ipa: /sə ʃofœʁ sə plɛ̃ suvɑ̃ dez‿ɑ̃butɛjaʒ/
notes: Ce the demonstrative and se the reflexive pronoun sound identical, so only grammatical role tells them apart.

fr: Il faut que tu prennes le premier train si tu veux arriver à l'heure.
en: You have to take the first train if you want to arrive on time.
ipa: /il fo kə ty pʁɛn lə pʁəmje tʁɛ̃ si ty vø aʁive a lœʁ/
notes: Prennes is the subjunctive after il faut que, ending in a silent es that sounds just like the indicative prend.

fr: Ces horaires ne sont plus valables depuis la grève.
en: These schedules are no longer valid since the strike.
ipa: /sez‿ɔʁɛʁ nə sɔ̃ ply valabl dəpɥi la gʁɛv/
notes: Ces the plural demonstrative sounds exactly like ses and c'est, so context alone decides the spelling.

fr: Quelle ligne dois-je prendre pour aller à la gare centrale ?
en: Which line should I take to go to the central station?
ipa: /kɛl liɲ dwaʒ pʁɑ̃dʁ puʁ ale a la gaʁ sɑ̃tʁal/
notes: Quelle the feminine form sounds identical to quel and quels, so gender agreement is silent but must be written.

fr: Bien qu'il pleuve, elle préfère aller au travail à vélo.
en: Even though it's raining, she prefers to go to work by bike.
ipa: /bjɛ̃kil plœv ɛl pʁefɛʁ ale o tʁavaj a velo/
notes: Pleuve is the subjunctive after bien que, with a silent final e that hides the change from the indicative pleut.

fr: Je doute que ce bus arrive avant midi.
en: I doubt this bus will arrive before noon.
ipa: /ʒə dut kə sə bys aʁiv avɑ̃ midi/
notes: Arrive in the subjunctive after je doute que looks identical to the indicative, so only douter signals the mood.

fr: C'est le dernier métro, ne le rate pas.
en: It's the last subway, don't miss it.
ipa: /sɛ lə dɛʁnje metʁo nə lə ʁat pa/
notes: C'est the contraction sounds exactly like ses and ces, so its apostrophe must be remembered though nothing is heard.

fr: Quel embouteillage incroyable aux heures de pointe !
en: What an incredible traffic jam during rush hour!
ipa: /kɛl‿ɑ̃butɛjaʒ ɛ̃kʁwajabl oz‿œʁ də pwɛ̃t/
notes: Quel liaises its silent l sound into the vowel of embouteillage, blending the exclamation into one sound group.

fr: Les usagers espèrent que la grève des transports se terminera bientôt.
en: Commuters hope the transport strike will end soon.
ipa: /lez‿yzaʒe ɛspɛʁ kə la gʁɛv de tʁɑ̃spɔʁ sə tɛʁminʁa bjɛ̃to/
notes: Se terminera keeps the reflexive se distinct from the future ending, even though the whole verb sounds smooth aloud.

fr: Bien que les prix aient augmenté, les gens continuent à prendre le train.
en: Even though prices have gone up, people keep taking the train.
ipa: /bjɛ̃ kə le pʁi ɛt‿oɡmɑ̃te le ʒɑ̃ kɔ̃tinɥ a pʁɑ̃dʁ lə tʁɛ̃/
notes: Aient is the subjunctive of avoir, pronounced like est or ai, so only the surrounding grammar reveals its spelling.

fr: Il est possible que le train soit annulé à cause de la neige.
en: It's possible the train will be cancelled because of the snow.
ipa: /il ɛ pɔsibl kə lə tʁɛ̃ swat‿anyle a koz də la nɛʒ/
notes: Soit is the subjunctive of être, and its final t liaises into the following vowel, blending it with annulé.

fr: Ses horaires de bus ont changé depuis septembre.
en: His bus schedules have changed since September.
ipa: /sez‿ɔʁɛʁ də bys ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃ʒe dəpɥi sɛptɑ̃bʁ/
notes: Ses the possessive sounds exactly like ces and c'est, so writers must rely on meaning rather than sound.

fr: Bien qu'elle soit pressée, elle attend patiemment son tour au guichet.
en: Even though she is in a hurry, she waits patiently in line at the counter.
ipa: /bjɛ̃kɛl swa pʁese ɛl atɑ̃ pasjamɑ̃ sɔ̃ tuʁ o giʃɛ/
notes: Soit here is subjunctive and elides smoothly with qu'elle, so the boundary between the words nearly disappears.

fr: Nous ne pensons pas que ce chemin soit plus rapide.
en: We don't think this route is faster.
ipa: /nu nə pɑ̃sɔ̃ pa kə sə ʃəmɛ̃ swa ply ʁapid/
notes: Ce chemin pairs the demonstrative ce with a noun, easily confused by ear with the reflexive se used before verbs.

fr: Quels que soient les horaires, elle arrive toujours en avance.
en: Whatever the schedule, she always arrives early.
ipa: /kɛl kə swat le ɔʁɛʁ ɛl aʁiv tuʒuʁ ɑ̃n‿avɑ̃s/
notes: Quels agrees in the plural with horaires, but the final s stays silent, so the agreement is invisible in speech.

fr: Le contrôleur veut que tous les passagers montrent leur billet.
en: The conductor wants all passengers to show their ticket.
ipa: /lə kɔ̃tʁolœʁ vø kə tu le pasaʒe mɔ̃tʁ lœʁ bijɛ/
notes: Montrent in the subjunctive keeps a silent ent ending identical to the indicative, so mood is only clear from context.

fr: C'est étonnant que le train soit encore en retard.
en: It's surprising that the train is late again.
ipa: /sɛt‿etɔnɑ̃ kə lə tʁɛ̃ swat‿ɑ̃kɔʁ ɑ̃ ʁətaʁ/
notes: C'est étonnant liaises the t of c'est into the following vowel, linking the two words smoothly in speech.

fr: Ce sont ses affaires qu'elle a oubliées dans le taxi.
en: Those are her belongings that she forgot in the taxi.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ sez‿afɛʁ kɛl a ublije dɑ̃ lə taksi/
notes: Oubliées agrees with the preceding direct object affaires placed before the verb, adding a silent es not heard aloud.

fr: Il vaudrait mieux que vous partiez plus tôt pour éviter la cohue.
en: It would be better if you left earlier to avoid the crowd.
ipa: /il vodʁɛ mjø kə vu paʁtje ply to puʁ evite la kɔy/
notes: Partiez is the subjunctive ending in iez, pronounced like parties without the s being heard.

fr: Quelle heure est-il ? Le dernier bus part dans dix minutes.
en: What time is it? The last bus leaves in ten minutes.
ipa: /kɛl œʁ ɛtil lə dɛʁnje bys paʁ dɑ̃ di minyt/
notes: Quelle heure liaises the silent final e of quelle away before the vowel of heure, joining the two words.

fr: Je crains que ce quai ne soit fermé pour travaux.
en: I'm afraid this platform is closed for construction.
ipa: /ʒə kʁɛ̃ kə sə kɛ nə swa fɛʁme puʁ tʁavo/
notes: Ce quai pairs the demonstrative with a masculine noun, sounding just like se would before a verb instead.

fr: Bien que le trajet soit long, elle préfère le train à l'avion.
en: Even though the journey is long, she prefers the train to the plane.
ipa: /bjɛ̃kə lə tʁaʒɛ swa lɔ̃ ɛl pʁefɛʁ lə tʁɛ̃ a lavjɔ̃/
notes: Soit stays invariable in the subjunctive regardless of subject, unlike the indicative est, though beginners expect agreement.

fr: Ses collègues prennent souvent le covoiturage pour économiser.
en: Her colleagues often carpool to save money.
ipa: /se kɔlɛg pʁɛn suvɑ̃ lə kovwatyʁaʒ puʁ ekɔnomize/
notes: Ses here is possessive and sounds identical to ces and c'est, so only meaning clarifies which spelling is correct.

fr: C'est dommage que les tarifs aient encore augmenté.
en: It's a shame that fares have gone up again.
ipa: /sɛ dɔmaʒ kə le taʁif ɛt‿ɑ̃kɔʁ‿oɡmɑ̃te/
notes: Aient the subjunctive of avoir sounds like est or ai, so recognizing the subjunctive trigger is the only clue.

fr: Quel que soit le trajet choisi, le prix reste le même.
en: Whatever route is chosen, the price stays the same.
ipa: /kɛl kə swa lə tʁaʒɛ ʃwazi lə pʁi ʁɛst lə mɛm/
notes: Quel que stays invariable before soit here, and beginners often confuse it with quelle que before a feminine noun.

fr: Nous aimerions que le nouveau tramway desserve notre quartier.
en: We would like the new tram to serve our neighborhood.
ipa: /nuz‿ɛməʁjɔ̃ kə lə nuvo tʁamwɛ desɛʁv nɔtʁ kaʁtje/
notes: Desserve is subjunctive, and its double s keeps a hard s sound, unlike a single s that would sound like z.

fr: Ce n'est pas parce qu'il pleut qu'elle prend sa voiture.
en: It's not because it's raining that she takes her car.
ipa: /sə nɛ pa paʁskil plø kɛl pʁɑ̃ sa vwatyʁ/
notes: Ce n'est pas begins with the demonstrative ce, easily confused with the reflexive se despite their different grammatical roles.

fr: Il semble que les horaires du dimanche aient changé.
en: It seems that the Sunday schedules have changed.
ipa: /il sɑ̃bl kə lez‿ɔʁɛʁ dy dimɑ̃ʃ ɛt‿ʃɑ̃ʒe/
notes: Aient changé liaises the t of aient into the vowel of changé, though the two words are grammatically separate.

fr: Ces retards répétés agacent tous les usagers du RER.
en: These repeated delays annoy all the RER commuters.
ipa: /se ʁətaʁ ʁepete agas tu lez‿yzaʒe dy ɛʁ ə ɛʁ/
notes: Ces plural demonstrative sounds identical to ses and c'est, so its meaning must be inferred from the plural noun retards.

fr: Je ne crois pas que ce soit la bonne station.
en: I don't think this is the right station.
ipa: /ʒə nə kʁwa pa kə sə swa la bɔn stasjɔ̃/
notes: Ce soit combines the demonstrative ce with the subjunctive of être, and both words blend together when spoken.

fr: Quelles solutions propose la mairie pour réduire les embouteillages ?
en: What solutions does the city propose to reduce traffic jams?
ipa: /kɛl sɔlysjɔ̃ pʁɔpoz la mɛʁi puʁ ʁedɥiʁ lez‿ɑ̃butɛjaʒ/
notes: Quelles agrees in the feminine plural with solutions, but the ending stays silent, so agreement is tracked in writing only.

fr: Bien qu'il soit tard, le bus circule encore dans le centre-ville.
en: Even though it's late, the bus still runs downtown.
ipa: /bjɛ̃kil swa taʁ lə bys siʁkyl ɑ̃kɔʁ dɑ̃ lə sɑ̃tʁəvil/
notes: Bien qu'il elides que before il, forming one blended sound that hides the boundary between the two words.

fr: C'est en marchant qu'elle a découvert ce raccourci vers la gare.
en: It was while walking that she discovered this shortcut to the station.
ipa: /sɛt‿ɑ̃ maʁʃɑ̃ kɛl a dekuvɛʁ sə ʁakuʁsi vɛʁ la gaʁ/
notes: C'est en liaises the t of c'est into the vowel of en, joining the emphatic construction into one sound group.

fr: Il faudrait que la ville construise plus de pistes cyclables.
en: The city should build more bike paths.
ipa: /il fodʁɛ kə la vil kɔ̃stʁɥiz ply də pist siklabl/
notes: Construise is the subjunctive form, ending in a silent e after the pronounced z sound, unlike the indicative construit.

fr: Ses amis lui ont conseillé de prendre le RER plutôt que le bus.
en: Her friends advised her to take the RER rather than the bus.
ipa: /sez‿ami lɥi ɔ̃ kɔ̃seje də pʁɑ̃dʁ lə ɛʁ ə ɛʁ plyto kə lə bys/
notes: Ses amis liaises the s of ses into z before the vowel of amis, and ses itself is a homophone of ces and c'est.

fr: Je suis content que le nouveau métro soit enfin ouvert.
en: I'm glad the new subway line is finally open.
ipa: /ʒə sɥi kɔ̃tɑ̃ kə lə nuvo metʁo swat‿ɑ̃fɛ̃‿uvɛʁ/
notes: Soit enfin ouvert chains two liaisons in a row, so the subjunctive verb blends into the words that follow it.

fr: Quel dommage que ce train direct n'existe plus.
en: What a shame that this direct train no longer exists.
ipa: /kɛl dɔmaʒ kə sə tʁɛ̃ diʁɛkt nɛgzist ply/
notes: Quel stays masculine singular here to agree with dommage, unlike quelle which a learner might wrongly expect.

fr: Bien qu'ils se plaignent des tarifs, ils reprennent le train chaque semaine.
en: Even though they complain about the fares, they take the train again every week.
ipa: /bjɛ̃kil sə plɛɲ de taʁif il ʁəpʁɛn lə tʁɛ̃ ʃak səmɛn/
notes: Ils se plaignent pairs the subject with the reflexive se, and the silent ent ending hides the plural subjunctive.

fr: C'est incroyable que ces horaires changent encore une fois.
en: It's unbelievable that these schedules are changing again.
ipa: /sɛt‿ɛ̃kʁwajabl kə sez‿ɔʁɛʁ ʃɑ̃ʒ ɑ̃kɔʁ yn fwa/
notes: C'est incroyable liaises c'est with the vowel of incroyable, while ces horaires hides another liaison right after it.
